name: Next Generation Diabetes Drugs
blurb: Triple agonists, amylin combinations and new oral GLP-1 pills.
title: Next Generation Diabetes Drugs
answer: The next wave acts on more than one hormone at once. Retatrutide targets GLP-1, GIP and glucagon receptors; amylin combinations pair a GLP-1 drug with an amylin analogue; and small molecule pills such as orforglipron deliver GLP-1 effects without injections or fasting rules. Only orforglipron is approved so far, and only for weight management.

explainer:
Adding hormones increases the effect. Glucagon, best known for raising blood sugar, also increases energy use and affects fat in the liver, so a drug that combines it with GLP-1 and GIP can drive weight loss beyond either alone while the incretin effects keep glucose in check. Amylin, released with insulin by beta cells, slows stomach emptying and increases fullness; combining an amylin analogue with a GLP-1 drug, as in Novo Nordisk's CagriSema or Lilly's EloraTZP, adds a second appetite signal.

Oral small molecules are the other frontier. Earlier oral semaglutide must be taken on an empty stomach with little water, 30 minutes before food. Orforglipron is a non-peptide molecule that avoids those rules. The trade off across the next generation is tolerability: greater effect usually brings more gastrointestinal side effects and more people stopping treatment.

developments.text: In the phase 3 TRIUMPH-2 trial in people with obesity and type 2 diabetes, retatrutide 12 mg produced 20.8 percent average weight loss over 80 weeks. It is not approved.
EloraTZP produced up to 23.3 percent weight loss and a 2.9 point A1C drop over 48 weeks in type 2 diabetes in a phase 2b trial, with phase 3 planned for late 2026.
The FDA approved Foundayo (orforglipron) for weight management, the first GLP-1 pill that can be taken any time of day without food or water rules.

In the phase 3 TRANSCEND-T2D-1 trial of 537 adults with early type 2 diabetes, retatrutide alone lowered A1C by 1.69 to 1.94 points and body weight by 11.5 to 15.3 percent over 40 weeks, against 0.81 points and 2.6 percent on placebo, with no severe hypoglycaemia. It remains investigational.

Amgen's MariTide, a monthly or less frequent injection combining GLP-1 activation with GIP blocking, is in phase 3 (MARITIME-1 and MARITIME-2, primary completion expected January 2027), with a type 2 diabetes phase 3 starting in 2026. No phase 3 results yet.
The New England Journal of Medicine published the trial of survodutide, Boehringer Ingelheim's once-weekly glucagon and GLP-1 dual agonist, in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes.

developments.text: Full results of retatrutide's phase 3 TRIUMPH-2 trial in obesity with type 2 diabetes appeared in The Lancet, and its obesity trial in the New England Journal of Medicine, the first peer reviewed phase 3 publications for the drug.
MannKind licensed technology to develop an inhaled, rapid acting, short duration GLP-1 for weight management with Rose Pharma.
Lilly called on online platforms, payment companies and regulators to shut down sales of illegal retatrutide, which is not approved anywhere.
Zealand Pharma's petrelintide, a human amylin analogue taken weekly, reported its randomised phase 2 obesity trial ZUPREME-1 in The Lancet Diabetes and Endocrinology.
A US multicentre trial of mazdutide, a glucagon and GLP-1 dual agonist, in adults with obesity or overweight was published.
Amgen registered a cardiovascular outcomes trial of MariTide (maridebart cafraglutide) and long term extension trials.
Long term safety results for oral orforglipron in Japanese people with type 2 diabetes (ACHIEVE-J) were published.
A GRADE assessed meta-analysis of randomised trials pooled the weight loss effect of CagriSema, semaglutide combined with cagrilintide.
